attempted_claim: Prove or disprove: there exist absolute constants C1,C2 such that for every epsilon in (0,1/2) and every integer k >= C1*epsilon^{-2}, any two graphons W,U:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] with max{|t(F,W)-t(F,U)|: F simple, |V(F)| <= k} <= exp(-C2*k^2) satisfy cut distance delta_square(W,U) <= epsilon. A complete answer either proves this polynomial-vertex inverse counting lemma with explicit C1,C2, or constructs an explicit infinite family of graphon pairs (W_k,U_k) with delta_square(W_k,U_k) >= epsilon0 > 0 for fixed epsilon0 while max_{|V(F)| <= k}|t(F,W_k)-t(F,U_k)| <= exp(-C2*k^2), with the density agreements and cut-distance separation verified rigorously.
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the polynomial-vertex inverse counting lemma was obtained; the spectral (R1), linear-response (R2), explicit-design (R3), and black-box boost (R4) routes were all concretely blocked, and the exhaustive check covers only n=3,4 block graphons with no asymptotic force.
